text:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: SEV1 triggered — spike in model-load failures in eu-central-1 warmup fleet. Lots of SIGKILL/container exits and 'deser: checksum mismatch' followed by cuda OOM on some pods. Paging oncall + runtime.

Oncall Bot: Paging Priya Patel (oncall) and Luis Ortega (runtime). Please ACK and join #incidents-bridge.

Priya Patel: ack. joining bridge now. who saw the first alarms?

Luis Ortega: saw it at ~09:42 UTC. Warmup controller logs show repeated attempts to load artifact v2.3.4. First failure is deserialization checksum mismatch then retry, then subsequent attempts hit high GPU mem and crash. Dump attached.

Luis Ortega: ```
[artifact-loader] shard=2 model=redwood-7b-v2 artifact=v2.3.4 status=deserialize error="checksum mismatch" attempt=1
[artifact-loader] shard=2 status=retrying
[loader] attempt=2 error="cudaMalloc failed: out of memory"
[kube] pod/warmup-xx-2 terminated exitCode=137
```

Kevin Park: infra alert — node pool eu-ctl-warmup-1 showing kernel OOM kills and memory fragmentation. 4/8 nodes showing >85% GPU memory reserved by orphaned processes. Possible warmup stampede + stale GVMM allocations.

Mary Li: CS reports two enterprise customers seeing increased 502s for session start. Customer docket IDs: CUST-889 and CUST-910. Both running on dedicated-us-eu region. Customer success opened priority channel.

OpsBot: Automatically disabled warmup-on-creation queue for eu-central-1 to prevent further stampede.

Priya Patel: good. Let's do triage steps:
1) Stop new warmups in eu-central-1 (OpsBot did that) 2) Identify and kill orphan GPU processes 3) Rollback artifact to v2.3.3 for active tenants 4) Evict+reboot unhealthy nodes 5) Customer comms.

Kevin Park: running GPU process sweep on the pool. Command: ```for node in $(list-nodes); do ssh $node 'pkill -f warmup || true'; done``` — starting now.

Luis Ortega: verifying loader config — artifact v2.3.4 introduced a change: larger shard alignment causing 10-20% more transient allocation during compile. That pushed some pods over available GPU budget when multiple shards compile concurrently. Also deserializer added checksum validation change that retries on mismatch which accidentally triggers full re-allocation.

Luis Ortega: reproducer steps attached. Repro shows transient spike to ~62GB on a 48GB GPU when two shards compile simultaneously.

Priya Patel: immediate mitigation: force artifact fallback for active tenants to v2.3.3. Also enable serialized load (one-shard-at-a-time) on warmup controller. Implementing now.

OpsBot: Applied tenant override for CUST-889 and CUST-910 to v2.3.3. Controller config patched: "warmup_serialization": "shard". Rolling config out to eu-central-1.

Mary Li: sending customers a high-touch note: "We're aware of session creation failures in EU; engineering has applied a temporary rollback and mitigations. No data loss. We'll update in 15m." CS will escalate to account teams.

Priya Patel: node remediation in progress — Kevin please cordon nodes showing fragmentation and initiate reboot sequence.

Kevin Park: cordoning nodes: runtime-eu-4 and runtime-eu-6. Reboot commands queued. Also bumping node GPU driver to include hotfix that clears persistent allocations on reboot.

Luis Ortega: also toggled runtime flag --deser-verify=false on warmup pods to avoid retry loop until we confirm artifact checksums. Note: we only disabled verify on warmup path, not on live serving.

Priya Patel: careful — turning off checksum verification could mask real corrupt artifacts. Confirmed we only did it on warmup pool and we will re-enable after validation.

OpsBot: warmup concurrency globally reduced to 1 per node in eu-central-1. That should avoid parallel compile spikes.

Luis Ortega: monitoring logs — after rollback to v2.3.3 and serial warmup, we still see occasional cudaMalloc OOM on a few legacy pods that weren't drained. Kicking drain now.

Priya Patel: draining legacy warmup pods, and forcing recreation with runtime:hotfix-eu that includes a smaller JIT cache and stream-deserialize logic.

Kevin Park: reboots finishing for runtime-eu-4; kernel reports freed GPU pages and no orphan processes now. Node back in rotation.

Mary Li: customer feedback: CUST-889 now reports sessions start successfully. CUST-910 still seeing intermittent 502s — appears they have pinned sessions on affected nodes; asking for tenant-level eviction.

Priya Patel: executing tenant eviction for CUST-910 and rescheduling their sessions to healthy nodes. Command run.

OpsBot: tenant eviction complete. Telemetry shows drop in 502s for CUST-910 to near baseline.

Luis Ortega: summary of root cause hypothesis: artifact v2.3.4 increased transient GPU allocations during compile + an aggressive checksum-retry path in warmup that caused multiple re-allocations; combined with warmup concurrency and some residual orphan allocations on nodes caused OOMs and container exits.

Priya Patel: status update: mitigations in place — rollback to v2.3.3 for active tenants, warmup serialization enabled, runtime hotfix rollout, node reboots and eviction for pinned tenants. Impact: two enterprise customers saw session start failures for ~20 minutes. Services restored for both after tenant eviction/rollback.

Mary Li: composing customer post-incident message: include timeline, what we changed, and that we're investigating artifact build-time memory estimates.

Luis Ortega: follow-ups assigned:
- add artifact memory usage estimator during CI (Luis)
- add pre-start resource check in warmup path to avoid launching compile when free GPU < threshold (Eng Runtime)
- revert deserialization verify toggle and implement exponential backoff instead of immediate retry on checksum mismatch (Luis)
- autoscaler should reserve warmup buffer capacity and limit concurrent compiles per node (Infra Kevin)

Priya Patel: handing off monitoring window to next oncall — @Kevin Park will shadow for 30 mins then escalate to Eng Runtime if alerts reappear. Handoff done. :thumbsup:

OpsBot: Incident marked RESOLVED for now. Logging timeline and creating postmortem placeholder: pm-6754321000.

IncidentBot: :memo: please add any additional notes to the postmortem doc. Thank you all for quick response.
